description: The World Input-Output Database provides world input-output tables that link the national input-output tables of major economies through bilateral trade, with underlying data such as socio- economic and environmental accounts. It was built by a consortium funded by the European Commission's 7th Framework Programme and, for the 2016 release, by the Dutch Science Foundation, and is now hosted by the Groningen Growth and Development Centre after the original wiod.org site was archived. The 2016 release covers 43 countries plus a model of the rest of the world for 2000 to 2014, with 56 sectors in ISIC Revision 4 and tables following the 2008 System of National Accounts; the 2013 release covers 40 countries for 1995 to 2011 with 35 sectors in ISIC Revision 3, and a long-run version exists. Tables and documentation are free downloads under CC-BY-4.0, with key papers by Timmer and colleagues to cite. Caveats: the project is no longer updated, so the latest year is 2014, and the country coverage leaves most developing economies in the rest-of-world aggregate. For simulation it is the economic network of inter-industry and inter-country flows used in input-output, supply-chain disruption and cascading-loss models. Related catalogue records include EXIOBASE, Eora2 and the FIGARO tables of Eurostat.
